When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training when I was 13, 14 years old. I had a very busy childhood, and sport was the solution to seek greater things in my life. In Amazonas there are a lot of jiu jitsu academies, so the sport is there for everyone, and the possibility of changing my life, too. If it weren't for sport, I would have lost myself in the world.

Training: Training is divided between Muay Thai, wrestling and physical preparation with technical days and sparring days.

What ranks and titles have you held? I was champion in numerous jiu jitsu competitions in the Amazon. In MMA, I was champion of the Amazon Talent event and Mr. Cage, having the belt of my category.

Do you have any heroes? My real hero was my grandfather. He was my father figure and he taught me to be a real man, may God bless him. In fighting, a guy I'm a fan of and I have the opportunity to be one of his sparring partners is Charles Oliveira, who is a sensational guy.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? The realization of a dream. I trained my whole life for this, I did all kinds of training and today being able to fight on the biggest stage in the world for me will be wonderful. God is wonderful! I'm coming and I'm going to carve my name in the organization.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked since childhood at the fair, selling fish, cheese, lemons, and whatever else could make money.

Favorite grappling technique: Arm lock

Favorite Striking technique: Flying knee

TRAINING: When training in Des Moines, I get woken up by kids instead of an alarm clock. After the kids are off to daycare, I get ready and head to the gym. Get my work/practice in, head home for a couple hours, then back to the gym. After practice it's usually doing some recovery stuff, then I head home usually around 6:30- 7pm. 

When and why did you start training for fighting? War is what I grew up with in Bosnia... Once we landed in America, I decided I wanted to make a positive career out of what I felt is normal and fun.

What ranks and titles have you held? Champion of MCC - Midwest Cage Championship
 
Do you have any heroes? Muhammad Ali and Bruce Lee
 
What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? My whole life has been about grooming for this moment and the most important time in my life. I couldn't be more excited, but all the work is just beginning.
 
Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No
 
What was your job before you started fighting? Mechanic, then I started my own business.
 
Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I started out fighting at a weekly event in Des Moines, IA (DMX fight night) and cleaned out everyone that came through the doors. I had to go pro because there was nothing left for me.
 
Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Beat two current UFC vets, Sam Alvey and Cezar Ferreira
 
Favorite grappling technique: Submitting my opponents by strikes or getting a takedown by knockout
 
Favorite Striking technique: However I get the knockout

Thoughts on upcoming opponent, Chris Haseman? Chris is a tough seasoned fighter. He is one of Australia’s MMA Pioneers so I know he has the experience. He will provide a tough and challenging match.

Training: The preparation for this match has been far from typical. I travelled to Thailand, where I worked on my standup for a couple of weeks. I then travelled to Dallas to work on my grappling. Finally, I ended up training in Las Vegas, the Mecca for MMA, where I put all my training together. I will then finalise my preparation at Sinosic Perosh Martial Arts here in Australia.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started to test myself to see if the years of training in the Martial Arts really meant anything.  This was in 1997.

What ranks and titles have you held? I hold Black Belts in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Shootfighting, Tae Kwon Do & Kai Shin.  I was also the Australian HW Vale Tudo Champion. I am also a multiple time Australian BJJ champion as well as Pan Pacific BJJ champion.

What is your favorite technique? Any submission.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? The UFC is the premier organization for MMA.  It means success in my training.  It means recognition for all my hard work.  It also means things just got harder.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I have a degree in Information Technology.

What was your job before you started fighting? I was an IT Support officer for a major international accounting firm. I now run a Martial Arts school with my business and training partner, Anthony Perosh.

TRAINING: Training in all aspects of MMA
 
When and why did you start training for fighting? After 10 years of training simply for the love of it, some of the youth in my therapeutic wilderness work inspired me to take my training to another level by fighting professionally. My MMA coach at the time, Marcus "The Irish Hand Grenade" Davis, was also very encouraging and he directed me to Jackson's MMA. At the tail end of 2009, I packed my car and drove cross country to Albuquerque to pursue a dream that grew larger than I could have ever imagined. Originally, with very few opportunities for women in the sport, my dream was limited to simply securing my first fight. As I continued to succeed, and opportunities for women continued to grow, my dream grew as well, and my love for training broadened as my training had a new and exciting purpose.
 
What ranks and titles have you held? None
 
Do you have any heroes? My (late) grandfather, Irving Kagan, is a hero to me for his relentlessness in the pursuit of success in all his endeavors. Among his achievements, he was an advocate for women in sports, he took a previously shunned sport (Freestyle Skiing) and brought it to the Olympics, he beat a heart attack and a high stage of Cancer, and claimed to have never had a mid-life crisis as he always felt "on top of the world."

I started fighting because throughout high school I got into a lot of fights in school. I was watching UFC and most of my friends would say, ‘You should start fighting. I bet you can make the UFC.’ I used to run a fight club in high school where about 30 kids would show up and we'd go at it with MMA gloves. We'd have like 15 fights every weekend with no hostility, just kids willing to go at it. It was all one on one. After high school I had no direction and just partied, but I wasn't happy, so I signed up for MMA as an amateur with no coach for my first three fights, where I practiced at my high school football field with my best friend, who had no knowledge of anything. I won my first three fights, then got picked up by my coach Ian Harris. I went 6-1 in one year of fighting, then went pro right after. 

What ranks and titles have you held? I'm a blue belt in jiu jitsu but roll at a much higher experience since I only do no gi. MMA jiu jitsu is different and that's why I'm successful in fighting on the ground. I had one title fight as a pro, but lost a decision, which was for Combate Global.

She migrated from Mexico and had to go through the border illegally. I was lucky to be born in the USA, but we did suffer, and I lived in a car as a toddler, so I lived a rough childhood, but it made me the fighter I am today. my mom is definitely the person who has made me who I am and my only hero.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? This has been my dream since I started and the only reason I wanted to do this. This feeling I have right now to know I have a contract and get to fight with a veteran, I'm on top of the world and can't wait to show what I am made of to everyone. I want to make my family proud and prove to everyone that hard work pays off. I started this journey seven years ago and I'm finally here, so I will show up ready for absolute chaos.
